_what_this_is: The forged church's FOUR material roles, one per slot on SM_Church_Forge_Split. Ruled option A 2026-08-30: a landmark justifies real per-material parameters, and a Z-blend cannot give the dome or the roof their own roughness and normal behaviour.
_slot_order_is_load_bearing: The roles map to the slots the splitter created, BY NAME: M_Church_Stone, M_Church_Plaster, M_Church_Copper, M_Church_Roof. scripts/blender/_archive/church_split.py (archived 2026-09-16, 1e) appends them in that order and the assignment is READ BACK after import -- the name is the binding, not the index.
_normal_convention: DX, matching recipes/c0_materials.json. derive_material_maps.py self-checks each derived normal against the height field it was built from and refuses if it does not read DX.

church_stone._roughness_base: Rough weathered stonework, essentially no specular sheen. Highest of the three.
church_stone._normal_strength: Strong: the base course is where relief reads at eye level, and rock_wall_08 is a deep-relief surface.
church_stone.source: Poly Haven CC0, fetched DIRECT from polyhaven.com -- NOT the .fbm copy. Byte-identical to it, which proves the provenance-by-filename claim.
church_stone._tile_m: MEASURED. Poly Haven publishes rock_wall_08 at 1800 x 1800 mm. This one was right first time because it was taken from the vendor rather than declared.

church_plaster._roughness_base: Lime plaster: matte, but slightly less so than raw stone.
church_plaster._normal_strength: Low. Plaster is nearly flat and a strong normal would invent a texture the concept does not show -- it describes CREAM PLASTERED WALLS, not render with visible aggregate.
church_plaster._tile_m: MEASURED, CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from a declared intent of 2.0 m. This albedo replaces Poly Haven's concrete_wall_003, published at 3000 x 3000 mm. Independently confirmed for the roof by counting the tile itself: ~36 shingle courses across 1024 px at a 0.18-0.22 m exposure is 6.5-7.9 m. The 1.5 m intent made tiling 5.3x too high, and the 'visible tile repetition' logged as an accepted trade-off was that error rather than a trade-off.

church_copper._roughness_base: LOWEST of the three, and this is the parameter that justified option A. Weathered copper still reads as metal: patina dulls it but it is not stone. A Z-blend across the whole church could not have given the dome a roughness distinct from the plaster below it, which is exactly the argument the operator made for the split.
church_copper._normal_strength: Lowest. A beaten metal sheet has shallow relief, and the placeholder's structure is borrowed from plaster -- pushing it hard would emboss plaster cracks onto a dome.
church_copper._placeholder: ⛔ NOT THE ARTEFACT OF RECORD. The operator is generating the real copper/patina tile. Structure is derived from plaster_wall_tiled; the COLOUR is invented, read off the concept's words ('WEATHERED COPPER ONION DOME, dark red-brown') and nothing else. Provenance in Free/_measured/copper_placeholder.json. RETIRES the moment the real tile lands -- delete this row's albedo, do not keep it as a fallback.
church_copper._tile_m: DECLARED INTENT and the only one left. The albedo is a PLACEHOLDER whose structure is borrowed from plaster_wall (measured 3.0 m) but which is meant to depict beaten copper sheet, so neither number is right. Provisional until the operator's tile lands.

church_roof._roughness_base: Weathered shingle: slightly less matte than lime plaster (0.82) because shingles hold a faint sheen when damp, and well above the copper's 0.55. Four distinct roughness values across four slots is what option A bought.
church_roof._normal_strength: High, second only to the stone. Shingle relief is the whole read of a roof at distance -- the concept calls for a WIDE SHINGLED ROOF WITH DEEP EAVES, and a flat normal would lose the course lines that make it legible.
church_roof.source: operator-generated, textures_v1, GRADED variant. grade_albedo.py moved roof_tiles toward the measured midpoint with the other graded roles, so it sits in the same tonal family as the plaster beside it.
church_roof._tile_m: MEASURED, CORRECTED 2026-08-31 from a declared intent of 1.5 m. This albedo replaces Poly Haven's grey_roof_01, published at 8000 x 8000 mm. Independently confirmed for the roof by counting the tile itself: ~36 shingle courses across 1024 px at a 0.18-0.22 m exposure is 6.5-7.9 m. The 1.5 m intent made tiling 5.3x too high, and the 'visible tile repetition' logged as an accepted trade-off was that error rather than a trade-off.

_roof_is_selected_by_normal: THE ROOF IS NOT A HEIGHT BAND. Stone, plaster and dome stack vertically so height separates them; the nave roof and the tower shaft occupy the SAME heights, so no horizontal cut separates those. The roof is selected by FACE NORMAL (signed up-component >= 0.55) inside the plaster height range. 0.55 sits in the measured trough between the wall mode (0.00-0.05, 42.91% of area) and the roof mode (0.60-0.70, 25.45%). Signed rather than absolute so a deep eave's SOFFIT -- as steep as the roof but facing down -- stays plaster instead of coming out shingled.
_tiling_is_derived: TILING IS COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED: tiling = metres_per_uv / tile_m, where metres_per_uv is MEASURED per slot by scripts/blender/church_uv_density.py and tile_m is declared above. The master carries a `Tiling` scalar that defaulted to 1.0 and that nothing ever set, so every role rendered at the machine unwrap's own scale -- one UV tile spanning ~50 METRES of building, which put shingle courses at half a metre and read as slate slabs. The unwrap itself is sound: density is near-uniform (50.3 / 50.5 / 53.3 / 54.3 m per uv across the four slots). Only the multiplier was missing.
